title: Part 61: Pilot Certification
description: Essential concepts for pilot certificates, ratings, privileges, limitations, and currency requirements

cards.back:
• Airplane/Rotorcraft: 17 years old
• Glider/Balloon: 16 years old

Remember: 'Sweet 16 for lighter-than-air, 17 for everything else'

• Airplane/Rotorcraft: 16 years old
• Glider/Balloon: 14 years old

Note: Student pilot certificate no longer has an expiration date (as of April 2016)

Required every 24 calendar months:
• Minimum 1 hour ground training (Part 91 review)
• Minimum 1 hour flight training
• Instructor endorsement in logbook

Alternatives that reset the clock: checkride, proficiency check, Wings program phase

Within preceding 90 days:
• 3 takeoffs
• 3 landings
• Same category, class, and type (if required)

Tailwheel: Must be to a full stop

Within preceding 90 days (1 hr after sunset to 1 hr before sunrise):
• 3 takeoffs
• 3 FULL-STOP landings
• Same category, class, and type (if required)

Memory aid: 'Night = 3 full stops'

Within preceding 6 calendar months:
• 6 instrument approaches
• Holding procedures
• Intercepting/tracking courses

Can be done in aircraft, simulator, or ATD
Memory aid: '6 and 6' (6 approaches in 6 months)

If IFR currency lapses:
• 6 additional calendar months to regain by doing required tasks
• After that: Instrument Proficiency Check (IPC) required

Total: 12 months before IPC mandatory

cards.front: Documents Required to Fly as PIC
cards.back:
Physical possession required:
1. Pilot Certificate
2. Photo ID (government-issued)
3. Medical Certificate (if required)

Memory aid: 'Pilot, Picture, Physical'

End of evening civil twilight → Beginning of morning civil twilight

• Civil twilight: Sun 6° below horizon
• Found in Air Almanac
• NOT the same as night currency period!

1 hour after sunset → 1 hour before sunrise

⚠️ Different from 'night' for logging time!

Memory aid: 'Currency needs padding-1 hour each side'

Minimum 40 hours total:
• 20 hrs dual instruction
• 10 hrs solo
• 3 hrs night (1 XC >100nm)
• 3 hrs instrument
• 3 hrs checkride prep (within 2 months)
• 5 hrs solo XC
• One 150nm XC (3 points, one >50nm)

Definition: Engine > 200 horsepower

Required to act as PIC:
• Ground training
• Flight training
• Logbook endorsement from authorized instructor

Definition:
• Retractable landing gear
• Flaps
• Controllable-pitch propeller (or FADEC)

Required: Ground training, flight training, endorsement

Note: No longer required for commercial checkride as of 2018

Type rating required for:
• Large aircraft (>12,500 lbs MTOW)
• Turbojet-powered aircraft
• Other aircraft specified by Administrator

Note: Even a private pilot needs these type ratings

To act as PIC above FL250:
• Ground training on physiology/operations
• Flight training (normal, abnormal, emergency)
• Logbook endorsement

Includes: Rapid decompression, emergency descent, use of equipment

May NOT fly for compensation or hire

Exceptions:
• Pro rata expense sharing (common purpose)
• Charity/community event flights
• Searching for missing persons
• Demonstration for sale (must have 200+ hrs)
• Aircraft salesman (logged 200+ hrs)

Private pilot may share operating expenses:
• Fuel, oil, airport fees, aircraft rental

Conditions:
• Must be common purpose
• Pilot pays pro rata share (no profit)
• Cannot 'hold out' to public

Must notify FAA within 30 days of permanent address change

Failure to notify: Cannot exercise certificate privileges

How: Mail, IACRA online, or FAA forms

Report to FAA within 60 days:
• Any motor vehicle conviction involving alcohol/drugs
• Administrative action (license suspension/revocation)

Two DUI convictions in 3 years = Certificate denial

Cannot act as crewmember:
• Within 8 hours of consuming alcohol
• With BAC ≥ 0.04%
• While under influence of alcohol
• While using any drug affecting safety

Memory aid: '8 hours bottle to throttle, 0.04 out the door'

Local solo endorsement: 90 days

Cross-country: Endorsement for each specific flight OR repeated flights to specific airports (90 days)

Valid for 120 days

Issued after passing practical test
Permanent certificate mailed to address on file

After revocation: Must wait 1 year before applying for any new certificate

After suspension: Certificate valid after suspension period ends

The person who:
1. Has final authority/responsibility for operation and safety
2. Has been designated as PIC before or during flight
3. Holds appropriate certificate and ratings

Only ONE PIC per flight

May log SIC time when:
• Required by type certificate
• Required by operating rules
• More than one pilot required by regulations

Must hold at least private pilot with category/class ratings

May log PIC when:
• Sole manipulator of controls AND rated for aircraft
• Acting as PIC (even if required pilot not rated)
• Student pilot solo
• Examiner conducting test

Note: Safety pilot may log PIC if acting as PIC

Category (broad): Airplane, Rotorcraft, Glider, Lighter-than-air

Class (within category): Single-engine land, Multi-engine sea, Helicopter, Gyroplane

Type (specific): B737, CL65, Citation

Remember: Category > Class > Type

Required to act as PIC of tailwheel aircraft:
• Ground training
• Flight training (normal/crosswind takeoffs & landings, wheel landings)
• Logbook endorsement

Note: Carries for life, no currency requirement beyond normal 61.57

• Age: 18 years old
• 250 hours total time
• 100 hours PIC
• 50 hours cross-country PIC
• Medical: Second class (for commercial privileges)
• Private pilot certificate or meet requirements

• Age: 23 years old (21 for restricted ATP)
• 1,500 hours total time (various reductions available)
• 500 hours cross-country
• 100 hours night
• 75 hours instrument
• First class medical required

Valid for 24 calendar months from month of issue

Renewal options:
• Activity (train students who pass checkride)
• FIRC (Flight Instructor Refresher Course)
• Practical test with examiner

Certificate: Pilot level (Student, Sport, Private, Commercial, ATP)

Rating: Added to certificate (Instrument, Multi-engine, Type)

Endorsement: Logbook authorization (Solo, Complex, High-performance, Tailwheel)

Valid for 24 calendar months

Must complete practical test within this period

If expired: Retake written test

Alternative to third-class medical:
• Hold valid driver's license
• Medical exam by state-licensed physician every 48 months
• Complete online course every 24 months
• No prior denial/revocation of medical

Limitations: 6 passengers, <250 kts, <18,000 ft, <6,000 lbs

When acting as safety pilot:
• At least private pilot certificate
• Category and class rating for aircraft
• Adequate vision forward and to sides
• Occupy seat with flight controls

May log SIC time; may log PIC if designated PIC

• 50 hours PIC cross-country
• 40 hours actual or simulated instrument time
• 15 hours instrument flight training
• Long IFR cross-country (250nm, 3 approaches)
• 3 hours within 2 months of checkride

Recent Experience (Currency): Regulatory minimums (3 takeoffs/landings, etc.)

Proficiency: Actual skill level-can be current but not proficient!

Good pilots exceed currency minimums

Before practical test:
• Pass knowledge test (within 24 months)
• Meet experience requirements
• Receive training endorsement (within 2 months)
• Hold required medical/student certificate
• IACRA application completed

Submit to FAA:
• Current certificate
• Copy of marriage license/court order/other legal document
• Completed application

May continue flying with old certificate until new one received

Foreign pilot with license from ICAO country:
• May obtain US private pilot certificate based on foreign license
• Limitations may apply
• Must read, speak, write, understand English
• FAA verification required
